paper_sections.title: Neural Correlates of Social Inclusion in Borderline Personality Disorder
Interaction effect of group and ball tossing condition

description.value: The study examined neural responses to social inclusion, exclusion, and passive watching during the Cyberball paradigm in females with borderline personality disorder, major depressive disorder, and healthy controls, and related BPD-associated activation differences to psychopathological characteristics.

design.value: A 3 × 3 group-by-condition fMRI design compared healthy controls, borderline personality disorder patients, and major depression patients across passive watching, inclusion, and exclusion conditions in the Cyberball paradigm. Differential inclusion-versus-passive-watching activation was compared between groups, with scanner type and age included as covariates.

name.value: Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-IV (SCID-I and -II)

description.value: Used to verify the clinical diagnoses of major depression and borderline personality disorder.
Assessed BPD symptom severity; total scores were divided by the number of items for further analyses.
Assessed current depressive symptoms in its German version.
A self-reporting questionnaire containing 30 items rated on a 4-point Likert scale; higher sum scores reflect higher trait impulsivity.

Assessed rejection sensitivity, defined as anxious expectation, ready perception, and overreaction to rejection cues; total scores were calculated by multiplying anxiety or concern scores by inverted expectancy of acceptance scores and dividing by the number of items.
Assessed general sensitivity for social exclusion with eight questions rated on a 5-point Likert scale; higher total scores correspond to higher sensitivity to social exclusion.

A 20-item scale assessing distress after social exclusion, comprising the subscales feeling excluded, low self-worth, meaningless existence, and control; items were rated from 1 (not at all) to 5 (very much).

name.value: feelings after fMRI visual rating scale

description.value: Subjective emotional experience regarding angry, sad, happy, afraid, frustrated, satisfied, helpless, and inner tension was rated from 1 (very low) to 4 (very strong) after the entire fMRI Cyberball paradigm.
Used to determine handedness.

task_description.value: Participants took part in a virtual ball-tossing game with two other participants who were supposed to be in another room. In fact, participants played against the computer and all actions were pre-programmed. Participants were represented by a hand at the bottom part of a screen, while the other players were represented by animated comic figures. Each of the three conditions was applied once and lasted around 2 min (60 throws).

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to take part in the virtual ball-tossing game with two other participants that were supposed to be in another room. During passive watching, participants were asked just to watch the game and the computer controlled their character.

stimuli.value: A virtual ball-tossing game displayed with the participant represented by a hand and the other players represented by animated comic figures.

description.value: Functional imaging data of the HC- and BPD-group were obtained with a 3T MAGNETOM Allegra. A T2*-sensitive gradient echo sequence was used for functional imaging with an echo time of 33 ms, a flip angle of 90°, a field of view of 230 mm, and a slice thickness of 2.5 mm with an interslice gap of 0.5 mm. At a repetition time of 2,000 ms, 35 transversal slices were recorded with an image size of 64 × 64 pixels during the cyberball task.

Functional imaging data of the MD-group were obtained with a 3T MAGNETOM Prisma Scanner. A T2*-sensitive gradient echo sequence was used for functional imaging with an echo time of 33 ms, a flip angle of 90°, a field of view of 230 mm, and a slice thickness of 2.5 mm with an interslice gap of 0.5 mm. At a repetition time of 2,000 ms, 35 transversal slices were recorded with an image size of 64 × 64 pixels during the cyberball task.
Anatomical high-resolution T1-weighted images were acquired for reasons of coregistration and normalization into standardized stereotactic space.

Data from each session were pre-processed including slice-timing, realignment, and normalization into a standard template (Montreal Neurological Institute, MNI) with a spatial resolution of 2 × 2 × 2 mm3. Smoothing was applied with an 8-mm FWHM isotropic Gaussian kernel. Intrinsic autocorrelations were accounted for by AR (1) and low frequency drifts were removed via high-pass filtering (1/128s).

model_settings.value: The cyberball task was modeled as three separate blocks of condition (passive watching, inclusion and exclusion). Regressors representing the six motion parameters were integrated into the design matrix. Intrinsic autocorrelations were accounted for by AR (1) and low frequency drifts were removed via high-pass filtering (1/128s). Beta-images representing the averaged, estimated magnitude of neural activation associated with passive watching, inclusion, and exclusion were computed for each participant.

model_type.value: 3 × 3 ANOVA model (omnibus F-test) with a random effects model for group analyses

model_settings.value: The two factors were group (HC, BPD, MD) and condition (passive watching, inclusion, exclusion), including first level contrasts for the three ball tossing conditions for each of the three groups. Scanner type and age were included as covariates in further analyses. Significant main effects were followed by single tailed t-interaction contrasts.
Parameter estimates of differential neural activation were extracted from significant clusters in the right dmPFC and PCC in BPD patients and correlated with individual BSL- and RSQ-scores.

A one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) and post-hoc Newman Keuls tests were computed to analyze psychometric scales. To control for multiple comparisons of the ANOVAs in dependent measures such as the NTS and the feelings after fMRI, a false-discovery rate (FDR) correction was applied at p < 0.05.

estimator.value: post-hoc Newman Keuls tests with false-discovery rate correction

title.value: Significant whole brain group-by-condition interaction effects and post-hoc analyses

caption.value: Significant (p < 0.001, k > 90 Vx corresponding to FWE-correction on cluster level) whole brain group-by-condition interaction effects and post-hoc analyses (p < 0.001, k > 150 Vx corresponding to FWE-correction on cluster level) comparing differential (inclusion vs. passive watching condition) neural activations between groups (HC, healthy controls; BPD, borderline personality disorder; MD, major depression) during the fMRI cyberball paradigm.
